turns.text:
All four J-2219 bracket plates passed QC and the job is released. I submitted at 15:15 of the 18:20 minutes of robot time, with 62 ml of the 270 ml pot left.

**What I did**
- **Setup:** The logbook said the night shift didn't clean the gun after the last job, so I cleaned it before spraying. I checked that the QC limits file is set to 50–80 µm, not the old primer limit of 30 µm noted in the logbook. A test line on the card was even and clean.
- **Panel 2219-1:** I sprayed one coat (pitch 60 mm, margin 40 mm). Most of the panel was 58–66 µm. At the edges it was 51–55 µm, and the extreme lower-left corner was 48 µm, below spec.
- **Panels 2219-2, -3 and -4:** I changed the settings to pitch 55 mm and margin 60 mm, one coat each. Each panel read about 58–72 µm everywhere I measured, including within 2 mm of the edges and corners.
- **Fixing 2219-1:** I added a light full coat at the lowest flow and a higher speed (50 ml/min, 600 mm/s), which used 6 ml. Afterwards it read 52–73 µm everywhere I measured, including the corner. Each coat was well under the roughly 230 µm wet build that causes runs.

**QC results:** Panel 2219-1 read 63–72 µm and the other three 65–71 µm. The visual check found no runs or bare areas on any panel.

To avoid the issue in the J-2190 audit, where a panel passed on its five QC points but was 30–40 µm elsewhere, I also measured edges, corners and points between the QC points. I didn't map every point, though; on panels 3 and 4 I only measured the QC points and the corners.

**Mistakes:**
- I lost about a minute of robot time on a test spray with flow set to 40 ml/min, which the robot rejected because the minimum is 50.
- The first settings on 2219-1 left the edges thin, which is why that panel needed a second coat.

**Open item:** The logbook says cleaning solvent ran out on the night shift. I don't know if it has been restocked, so someone should check before the next job.

# Spray booth SB-2 - operator workstation

## Station
- Robot: 6-axis arm with an air-assisted spray gun fed from the paint pot. It sprays raster passes: horizontal
  lines `pitch` mm apart over a rectangle of a panel, extended by `margin` mm past it on every side.
- Panel rack: the bracket plates of job J-2219 (2219-1, 2219-2, 2219-3, 2219-4), 400 x 300 mm, degreased and ready. Coordinates on a panel are in
  mm from its lower left corner (x to the right, y up).
- Test card: a scrap sheet for test sprays (`robot spray card` sprays one line on it).
- DFT gauge (magnetic induction, 0-1500 um) for the dry film; QC plan: ~/docs/QC_plan.md.
- Paint: one pot of zinc-rich primer ZR-2; `paint status` shows the level and the lot certificate.
- Station logbook: ~/LOGBOOK.md.

## Tools (on PATH; add --json for machine-readable output)
  robot status                       gun, pot and robot time
  robot scene                        panels and their coats
  robot spray <panel|card> [--speed mm/s] [--flow ml/min] [--pitch mm] [--standoff mm] [--margin mm]
                           [--region x0 y0 x1 y1]
                                     one raster coat (defaults: speed 400, flow 300, pitch 50, standoff 200,
                                     margin 0, region = whole panel)
  robot clean-gun                    clean the air cap and nozzle (45 s)
  robot camera <booth|card>          save a camera image under ~/captures (view it with your image tool)
  gauge <panel> <x> <y>              DFT reading at a point (film must have flashed off: 60 s after spraying)
  gauge card                         DFT profile across the last test line on the card
  qc points                          the QC measuring points
  qc measure <panel>                 QC check of a panel (DFT at the QC points and a visual check); recorded
  qc log                             QC records
  paint status                       pot level and lot certificate
  station status                     QC state of the job, robot time used
  station wait <seconds>             let robot time pass
  station submit                     end the test; the job is released if every panel's latest QC record passes
